tagline: Down the Catawba Valley, mill name by mill name.
intro: From Lusters Gate, Catawba Road runs along the floor of the Catawba Valley past Bennetts Mill and McDonalds Mill, two places that each kept a country post office for a generation or more in the 1800s. At McDonalds Mill the valley lies between Paris Mountain to the south and Gallion Ridge to the north.
The road is part of U.S. Bicycle Route 76, the TransAmerica route, and it ends at Route 311 in Catawba, a farming community in the valley just over Catawba Mountain from the Roanoke Valley.

moments.title: McDonalds Mill
moments.text: George McDonald ran a mill here, and a post office called McDonalds Mills sorted the valley's mail from 1847 until 1913.

moments.title: Catawba
moments.text: Among the valley farms, the state's Catawba Hospital traces its start to an 1857 resort set up to use a sulfur and limestone spring believed to heal.

moments.title: McAfee Knob
moments.text: Four miles up the Appalachian Trail from Route 311, this knob, named for a settler of the late 1730s, looks down 1,600 feet on the Catawba Valley.
